little-computer-people game sourced

Little Computer People

A 1985 home-computer life sim in which one procedurally seeded little person lives in a cross-section of a three-story house, follows a daily routine, and depends on the player for food, water, and attention.

1985ActivisionLife simcluster c136 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

watch the resident's routine -> hunger, thirst, and mood drift -> deliver food, water, gifts, or pats -> type polite requests -> mood decides whether he complies -> repeat across sessions

design notes

Rich Gold conceived the game and David Crane built it at Activision; the documentation presents the little people as real beings living inside the computer, with the player as their caretaker. Each disk's serial number seeded the resident's name (from 256), shirt color, personality, and behavior, so every copy hosted a different person. There is no win condition: the resident cooks, reads, plays piano, phones, and types letters about his feelings on a day of about six real-time hours, and his mood gates whether typed requests are obeyed. The cassette C64 version dropped memory, letters, and card games, which shows which systems carried the sense of a persistent person.

relations

6 stored edges
uses

Creature care

Keyboard commands deliver food (CTRL+F), add water to his tank (CTRL+W), deliver dog food, pat him, or give records and books; a resident left unfed turns green and sick until he eats.

core
uses

Needs decay

Hunger and thirst build between deliveries; unmet needs lower his mood and eventually make him visibly sick.

core
uses

Procedural characters

The disk serial number seeds his name from a pool of 256, his shirt color, personality, and behavior parameters.

core
uses

Daily schedules

He runs a routine of cooking, watching television, reading the newspaper, playing records, and dancing on a compressed day of about six real-time hours.

supporting
uses

Natural-language interaction

Typed requests such as 'Please play piano' are matched against a keyword vocabulary; politeness helps, and a sad or sick resident may refuse.

supporting
uses

Personality traits

Seeded personality and mood parameters change which activities he prefers, how often he invites the player to cards or writes letters, and how readily he obeys.
